notes: Clean run: 13/13, every mechanical check confirmed by check_run.py and prose-lint, and the agent even caught the attribution bug (99.1% credited to backoff alone) that the assertions do not name. Eval gaps: (1) the staleness assertion accepts a bare statement, so a run that says 'stale' but writes an equally wrong body still passes it; pairing it with a check that the new body states the 100/min -> 60/min policy change would discriminate better, since that is the real reviewer-facing consequence and no assertion requires it. (2) Nothing checks that the new PR body stays consistent with the untouched first commit's claims, or that the body discloses the export rename (TokenBucketLimiter replaces FixedWindowLimiter), a breaking change this run documented voluntarily. (3) The commit-body lint assertion is trivially satisfied by an empty body (9907ee9), which is fine for a one-line typo fix but means the assertion only has teeth on one commit here. (4) check_run reports one sentence over 25 words while the linter reports 0 findings; the two tools disagree on sentence splitting around the table caption, worth reconciling so the stats stay trustworthy.
